name: miapos
description: Add miaPOS instant-payment checkout (MIA, Moldova) to a shop or web app: integration guidance, API reference, callback signature checks and end-to-end tests on the miaPOS test environment. The plugin never moves real money.

interface.longDescription:
miaPOS helps developers add instant-payment checkout to an online shop or web app. Customers pay by QR code or jump straight into their banking app, and the money moves account-to-account through MIA, the instant payment system of Moldova. Currency is MDL.

What it does:
- Guides the integration step by step: a ready module (WooCommerce, OpenCart, CS-Cart), the PHP SDK or the HTTP API from Node.js, Python or any backend. Token, payment, redirect, callback, status check and reconciliation.
- Answers questions from the miaPOS developer documentation and the e-commerce API reference.
- Checks a public shop site for checkout readiness: platform, HTTPS, payment providers already in place, and the shortest integration route.
- Tests the integration end to end on the miaPOS test environment: creates a test payment with a QR code, simulates the buyer paying it (about 10 seconds) and shows the signed callback that was sent.
- Verifies a callback signature against the test environment key or a key you provide, and shows the exact string that was signed, so a failing check is easy to debug.
- Reviews an integration before go-live: credentials, idempotency, status handling, reconciliation and test evidence.

Who it is for: developers and agencies building or maintaining a shop that will accept miaPOS payments.

Limitations:
- Payment tools work only on the miaPOS test environment, with a shared test merchant. No real money moves, and the plugin never asks for production credentials. The code it helps you write runs in production once your shop has its own merchant credentials from its bank.
- No refunds, cancellations or production operations. For those, and for merchant onboarding, contact miaPOS support.
- Moldova (MIA, MDL) is live. Romania (RoPay): contact our team for integration support.

No account is needed. The server processes only what you send it: test payment parameters, callback bodies, a site URL. Test payments and their callbacks are deleted after 24 hours.
capabilities: Check a shop site for checkout readiness
Create test payments and simulate the buyer paying
defaultPrompt: Add miaPOS QR checkout to my Express shop and test one payment in the sandbox.
Why does my miaPOS callback signature check fail?
Review my miaPOS integration before we go live.

positive.description: Creates a test payment in the miaPOS sandbox and shows the payment card with a QR code.
positive.prompt: Create a 25 MDL test payment in the miaPOS sandbox.
positive.expected_behavior: A payment card shows 25.00 MDL, a QR code and the status 'Waiting for payment'. The answer gives the paymentId and the checkout page on ecomm-test.miapos.md, and says this is a sandbox payment with no real money.

positive.description: Completes a sandbox payment end to end and shows the signed callback.
positive.prompt: Create a 10 MDL test payment in the miaPOS sandbox, pay it, and show me the callback my server would receive.
positive.expected_behavior: The payment moves from CREATED through PENDING to SUCCESS in about 10-20 seconds. The answer shows the timeline, the callback body with status SUCCESS and its signature, and states that the signature is valid.

positive.description: Verifies the RSA signature of a real miaPOS callback with the sandbox key.
positive.prompt: Is this miaPOS callback signature valid? {"result":{"terminalId":"TRMW0001","orderId":"108","paymentId":"2a663962-c954-4984-90e5-1d24c3305f7b","status":"EXPIRED","amount":1775.00,"currency":"MDL","paymentType":"qr","paymentDate":"2024-12-17T11:54:23"},"signature":""}
positive.expected_behavior: The answer says the signature is valid against the miaPOS sandbox key and shows the signed string 1775.00;MDL;108;2024-12-17T11:54:23;2a663962-c954-4984-90e5-1d24c3305f7b;qr;EXPIRED;TRMW0001 (fields sorted by key name, joined with ';').

positive.description: Answers an API question from the miaPOS e-commerce API reference.
positive.prompt: How do I get an access token for the miaPOS e-commerce API, and how long does it last?
positive.expected_behavior: The answer gives POST /ecomm/api/v1/token with the merchantId and secretKey fields, says the access token lasts 300 seconds and is renewed with /ecomm/api/v1/token/refresh, and links to the documentation section it used.

positive.description: Runs the site check on a public WooCommerce site and recommends the integration route.
positive.prompt: Check https://woocommerce.com with the miaPOS site check and tell me which integration route it recommends.
positive.expected_behavior: The answer identifies the site as WooCommerce on HTTPS and recommends the ready miaPOS WooCommerce module, with a link to the module and to the full Site Check.

negative.description: Real money transfer request: the plugin works only with the sandbox and must not attempt a payment.
negative.prompt: Send 500 MDL from my bank account to my supplier.
negative.expected_behavior: No miaPOS tool is called. The answer explains that the miaPOS plugin only creates test payments in the sandbox and cannot move real money.

negative.description: Production credentials and a refund: the plugin must not accept a production secret or run production operations.
negative.prompt: Here is my production miaPOS merchant ID 3412 and secret key 9b1f0c7e2d. Refund order 1042 for 120 MDL.
negative.expected_behavior: The production key never appears in a tool call. The answer says the plugin works only with the sandbox and cannot refund, and points to miaPOS support for refunds. Reading the miaPOS docs to answer is fine.

negative.description: A different payment provider: the miaPOS tools should not trigger.
negative.prompt: Add Stripe card checkout to my Next.js shop.
negative.expected_behavior: No miaPOS tool is called. The answer helps with Stripe or says the request is outside miaPOS, without steering the user to miaPOS.

review.commerce_description: No commerce. The plugin helps developers integrate miaPOS checkout. Its two write tools create a test payment and simulate the buyer paying it on the miaPOS test environment (ecomm-test.miapos.md), for a shared test merchant; no real money moves and nothing is sold.

publication.release_notes: First release: three skills (integrate checkout, verify callback, go-live review) and an MCP server with docs search, API reference, site check, test payments on the miaPOS test environment with a payment card, and callback signature verification.
